subject: a97A02:B1 — what the window integral means near the endpoints of [0,1]

nodes.claim: The problem defines f on [0,1] only; what does the integral over [t-h, t+h] mean when t is within h of an endpoint?

Integrating f against Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,1] is the same as integrating the zero extension of f against Lebesgue measure: the part of the window outside [0,1] contributes nothing either way, so the average is over the part of the window inside the interval.
The problem's f is read as a function on R that vanishes outside [0,1].

For any measurable set A, the integral of f over A against volume restricted to [0,1] equals the integral over A of the zero extension against volume, because the restriction multiplies the integrand by the indicator of [0,1].
The average f_h(t) is the integral of f over [t-h, t+h] ∩ [0,1], divided by 2h.
